intro: To add header rows in Numbers on Mac, select the table, open the Format sidebar, click Table, and set Headers & Footer to the number you want. Each table allows up to five header rows, and Apple's shortcut list has none for this step.
tldr: Click a cell in the table, open the Format sidebar, then click Table.
Under Headers & Footer, pick the number of header rows. Choose 0 to remove them.
Numbers allows up to five header rows per table.
The existing top row becomes a header and keeps its data.
For an empty header, insert a blank row above with ⌥↑ first.

blocks.text: Header rows repeat your labels at the top of a table, such as Region, Month and Sales. They stay in place when you scroll, once you freeze them. In Numbers on Mac, the setting lives in the Format sidebar. Some older guides show a menu bar path instead, and that path is out of date.
What a header row does in a Numbers table

A header row is the top row, or rows, that Numbers treats as labels. You can have up to five of them in one table. The same limit applies to header columns on the left side. Footer rows sit at the bottom of the table, and you can have up to five of those too. A typical table needs one header row, so start with one and add more only when you need them.
Check your Numbers version before you follow the steps

Apple's current Numbers for Mac guide covers Numbers 15.4. To check your version, open the Numbers menu and choose About Numbers. Numbers 15.1 came out in January 2026 as a standalone app under Apple Creator Studio. TidBITS says version 15.1 needs macOS 15.6 Sequoia or later. Older 14.x releases were not checked, so treat these steps as confirmed for 15.x only.
Where the setting lives: Format sidebar, Table tab, Headers & Footer

The Table tab only shows table settings when a table is selected. Once it does, the Headers & Footer section holds three pop-up menus. One sets header rows, one sets header columns, and one sets footer rows. Each menu takes a number. Choosing 0 removes that kind of header or footer. Freeze Header Rows and Freeze Header Columns sit in the same menus, so the freeze setting lives in the same place.

rows: Turns top rows into labels, which can be frozen
Turns left columns into labels, which can be frozen
Adds rows at the bottom, often for totals
Removes that kind of header or footer

blocks.text: Worked example: a table that needs an empty header row

Say your table has three columns, Region, Month and Sales, and the first row holds data for one region. If you set header rows to one now, that data row becomes the header. The data stays, but the row now acts as a label. This is the part that catches people out.

To keep an empty header, click a cell in the top row and press ⌥↑. Numbers adds a blank row above it. Then set the header rows menu to one. Apple describes the top row converting to a header, so the blank row should become the header, and you type your labels into it. Apple does not show this exact workflow, so check the result on your own table before you rely on it.
Freeze header rows so the labels stay on screen

Freezing keeps the header visible while you scroll through a long table. Choose Freeze Header Rows in the same Headers & Footer menu. Deselect it to unfreeze. Freeze Header Columns works the same way for the left side, which helps on a wide table you scroll sideways. Apple's guides list both options in these pop-up menus.

items: Scroll down a long table. The header should stay at the top of the window.
If the header scrolls away, open the Headers & Footer menu and confirm the freeze option has a checkmark.
Scroll sideways on a wide table to test Freeze Header Columns.
If the freeze stops holding after an update, use the troubleshooting steps below.

blocks.text: When to use header columns and footer rows

Use header columns when your first column holds names or categories you want visible while you scroll sideways. Use footer rows for totals or notes at the bottom. Turn them on only when the table needs them. Each one adds a row or column of labels, so extra headers can make a small table feel crowded.
Why a header row will not sit in the middle of a table

Header rows only work at the top of a table. An Apple Community answer says a header row in the middle is not a true header. The workaround in that thread is to change the fill colour of that row so it stands out. That answer comes from a user, not from Apple's docs, so treat it as a workaround.

blocks.title: Community tips, not Apple docs
blocks.text: The arrow beside a row number, the plist reset, and the Table menu path all come from Apple Community threads. Apple's current docs do not list them. Try the documented Format sidebar steps first.
Rows slide under the header: what to try

One Apple Community thread describes rows 2, 3 and 4 sliding under row 1. The top reply says to turn off header rows in Inspector > Format > Table > Headers and Footers. Another reply suggests dragging the table's top-left handle back onto the page. That thread is about Numbers on iPadOS 26, so test the fix on your Mac and check the result.
How header rows help when you sort and filter

Header rows tell you what each column holds before you sort or filter. When you sort by a column, the label row helps you confirm you picked the right one. Short, specific labels such as Region or Sales are easier to read at a glance. Keep labels consistent across the table so the header always matches the data below it. The sort and filter guides linked below show the exact steps.
Common mistakes with header rows in Numbers

items: Looking for Table > Header Rows in the menu bar. Apple's current docs do not show that path. It comes from an older Numbers 5.1 thread.
Expecting an empty header row after you choose one. The top row converts and keeps its data.
Expecting freeze to happen on its own. Freeze Header Rows is a separate choice in the same menu.
Trying to put a header in the middle of the table. Header rows only work at the top.
Selecting a chart or text box instead of the table. Click a cell inside the table first.

blocks.text: Numbers for iCloud uses the same path

In Numbers for iCloud, click the table, then click Table at the top of the Format sidebar. Click the Headers & Footer pop-up menus and choose a number of header rows. Apple's iCloud guide lists the same five-row limit and the same freeze options. That guide is a separate document from the Mac guide. Apple's docs show no web-only differences, but check the menus on your own screen.
What to do next with your table

If you do not have a table yet, start with [How to add a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/add-a-table-in-numbers). Once your header is set, sort the rows below it with the steps in [How to sort a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/sort-a-table-by-column-in-numbers). If you need to narrow down rows, follow [How to filter a table in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/filter-table-rows-in-numbers). For faster row edits, see [How to use keyboard shortcuts in Numbers on Mac](/how-to/use-keyboard-shortcuts-in-numbers).

faq.question: Why is there no Table > Header Rows menu in Numbers on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's current Numbers docs put header settings in the Format sidebar, under the Table tab. The Table > Header Rows path appears in an older Numbers 5.1 community thread. Use the Format sidebar instead.

faq.question: How many header rows can a Numbers table have?
faq.answer: Up to five header rows, five header columns and five footer rows per table, according to Apple's guides for Numbers on Mac and Numbers for iCloud.

faq.question: Does adding a header row delete my first row?
faq.answer: No. Adding header rows converts the existing top row into a header and keeps its data. If you want an empty header, insert a blank row above first with ⌥↑.

faq.question: How do I remove a header row?
faq.answer: Select the table, open the Format sidebar, click Table, and set the Headers & Footer menu to 0. Apple says a setting of 0 removes the headers.

faq.question: Can I freeze the header row so it stays visible?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose Freeze Header Rows from the Headers & Footer pop-up menu. Deselect it to unfreeze. If the freeze stops holding after an update, see the troubleshooting list on this page.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut for header rows in Numbers?
faq.answer: Not in Apple's current shortcut list. The shortcuts ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ add rows above or below, but they do not make a header. Use the Format sidebar to set header rows.

faq.question: Can I put a header row in the middle of a table?
faq.answer: No. Header rows only work at the top. An Apple Community answer suggests changing the fill colour of the row so it stands out as a label.

faq.question: Do the same steps work in Numbers for iCloud?
faq.answer: Apple's iCloud guide uses the same path. Click the table, click Table at the top of the Format sidebar, then use the Headers & Footer menus. Check your own screen, because the iCloud guide is a separate document.

faq.question: Which Numbers version do these steps cover?
faq.answer: Apple's current Mac guide covers Numbers 15.4. Check your version under Numbers > About Numbers. Older 14.x releases were not checked for these steps.

task: Add header rows to a table in Numbers on Mac
appliesTo: Numbers 15.x for Mac, using the Format sidebar Table tab
requirements: Numbers 15.x for Mac. Apple's current guide covers Numbers 15.4.
A table in your spreadsheet, selected by clicking a cell inside it.
For Numbers 15.1, macOS 15.6 Sequoia or later.
Your data open, so you can check the top row after the change.

steps.name: Select the table
steps.text: Open your spreadsheet in Numbers and click any cell inside the table. Table settings only appear in the Format sidebar when a table is selected.
steps.tip: If you click a chart or text box by mistake, the Table tab will not show your table settings.

steps.name: Open the Format sidebar
steps.text: Click the Format button in the toolbar at the top of the window. It looks like a paintbrush. The sidebar opens on the right side of the window.

steps.name: Click the Table tab
steps.text: At the top of the Format sidebar, click Table. The table settings appear, with a Headers & Footer section further down.

steps.name: Find the Headers & Footer pop-up menus
steps.text: Scroll to the Headers & Footer section. Click the pop-up menu for header rows. The menu offers numbers from 0 up to 5.

steps.name: Choose the number of header rows
steps.text: Pick 1 for a single header row. Apple allows up to five header rows per table. Pick 0 later if you want to remove the header.
steps.tip: Start with one header row, then add more only if you need them.

steps.name: Check the top row
steps.text: The existing top row becomes the header and keeps its data. If you wanted an empty header instead, insert a blank row first, as in the next step.

steps.name: Insert a blank row for an empty header (optional)
steps.text: Before you change the header count, click a cell in the top row and press ⌥↑. Numbers adds a blank row above it. Set the header rows menu to 1, then type your labels into the new header.
steps.tip: Apple lists ⌥↑ for adding a row above. It does not add a header by itself.

steps.name: Turn on Freeze Header Rows (optional)
steps.text: In the same Headers & Footer menu, choose Freeze Header Rows. The header stays visible when you scroll. Deselect it to unfreeze the rows.

steps.name: Add header columns or footer rows if needed
steps.text: Use the other Headers & Footer menus for header columns and footer rows. Each allows up to five. Freeze Header Columns sits in the same menu as the header column setting.

shortcuts.action: Add a row above the selected cells
Add a row below the selected cells

troubleshooting.problem: The Headers & Footer section is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Click a cell inside the table, not a chart or text box. Then open the Table tab again. The section only shows for a selected table.

troubleshooting.problem: Rows 2 to 4 slide under the header row
troubleshooting.fix: Turn header rows off, or drag the table's top-left handle back onto the page. The thread reporting this is about iPadOS 26, so test on your Mac first.

troubleshooting.problem: Freeze Header Rows does not hold after an update
troubleshooting.fix: Turn Freeze Header Rows off, restart Numbers, then turn it on again. Some users also move com.apple.Numbers.plist to the Desktop. Keep a copy of any file you move. This is user-reported, not an Apple fix.

troubleshooting.problem: A header row sits in the middle of the table
troubleshooting.fix: Header rows only work at the top. Change the fill colour of that row so it stands out as a label instead.

troubleshooting.problem: The menu bar has no Table > Header Rows item
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected in current Numbers. The menu path comes from an older Numbers 5.1 thread and is outdated. Use the Format sidebar instead.

troubleshooting.problem: My first data row became a header
troubleshooting.fix: This is expected. Adding header rows converts the top row and keeps its data. Next time, insert a blank row above with ⌥↑ first.
